client_context.contact: Mr. Minh (Vietnamese, connection of CEO, oversees 30+ English centers in Hanoi/Saigon)
client_context.ceo_demand: Basic communication over grammar/IELTS. Broken English = fine. No big smart sentences. Get to the point directly.

core_principles.name: KISS
core_principles.quote: KISS which is keep it simple stupid. Broken English that communicates > perfect grammar that freezes. Get to the point. Directly. Even if it's broken.

core_principles.name: Two Brains
core_principles.quote: You got your Vietnamese brain, uh which is if you're a native speaker of Vietnamese, that's your stronger brain, and then you got your English brain, which is a brain you're trying to develop. And if you try to bridge the English brain or your weaker brain with the Vietnamese, uh as a handicap, it actually handicaps you and stops you from being able to progress because you can't learn English while thinking in Vietnamese because they're completely different languages and they require different parts of the brain.

core_principles.name: Mistakes = Guideposts
core_principles.quote: Mistakes are good because they show you 'oh, this is not the right way. Okay, then this must be the right way.' Mistakes are guideposts.

core_principles.name: Laugh at Yourself
core_principles.quote: Learn to laugh at yourself. Learn to not take yourself so seriously.

core_principles.name: Bruce Lee Vocabulary Rule
core_principles.quote: It's not about knowing 10,000 vocabulary. It's about knowing 500 to 1,000 vocabulary and knowing how to use each vocabulary in 10 different situations. That's what makes you a dynamic speaker and somebody who can communicate effectively and simply.

core_principles.name: Comprehensive Input
core_principles.quote: Anything they are passionate about. But the rule is they have to at least understand 60%. If they don't understand 60% they must choose new material or they're permitted to use English subtitles. Vietnamese subtitles are absolutely forbidden for the same two brain kind of problem that we discussed before.

class_rules_student_facing: No Vietnamese — not even one word. If you're thinking in Vietnamese, you're freezing. Banned for the full 90-minute session.
No notebooks, no scripts — if you wrote it down, you're not listening. Crutch. It distracts you from active listening.
No phones — translation apps and TikTok kill active listening. Leave it outside. The only person allowed to use translate is the teacher, and only after 3 attempts to explain from different angles.
listening_rules: 1 hour per day: 45 minutes active listening + 15 minutes speaking
Material must be 60% comprehension minimum. Below 60% = switch to easier content or English subtitles
Notebooks are banned during listening time too — no pausing to look up words
Learn vocabulary like a child: hear it repeatedly in context, let the brain build the connection naturally
Only add words that show up 4-5 times across different situations — that's a useful word
teaching_rules: Try at least 3 times from 3 different angles to explain a vocabulary or concept before using translate. Translate is a tool, not a crutch.
Filter out nonsense words from class transcripts. Only highlight core vocabulary that fits KISS principle.
Students can jot words on phone AFTER listening session ends — not during. Passive vs active listening distinction.

conversation_technique.framework: WWWWH — Who, What, Where, When, How, Why
conversation_technique.quote: When you can find out why someone does something, you know why somebody gets out of bed in the morning, why they work so hard. You can find what their passion is, and when you can find out what their passion is, you can have them talking for hours.
conversation_technique.universal_topic_principle: Everybody's favorite topic is themselves. Even people who seem selfless — they are selfless because it makes them feel good. Because they love their family, which is an extension of themselves. This is not selfishness. This is life.
conversation_technique.follow_up_importance: The weakest area with their question was lack of follow-up questions. It's the follow-up question that allows you to continue to dig deeper. If you're just surface level asking questions and retreating back to your pre-defined, scripted list of questions, then you're always going to stay shallow.

student_weaknesses_identified: Lack of follow-up questions — ran out of questions fast using pre-written scripts
Mental translation from Vietnamese → English causes total freeze. Takes all the RAM. Recipe for disaster.
Perfectionism — need to be perfect before speaking, need to know everything before beginning
Fixating on unknown words instead of listening to what they do know
cultural_notes_vietnamese_students: Fear of losing face / making mistakes in public is the biggest social fear
Raised whole life thinking any mistake is bad — need to reframe mistakes as healthy/good
Don't take themselves seriously — need to learn to laugh at themselves
Need to be perfect before they can get started — need to learn to walk as far as they can see, then see further
Vietnamese deflect compliments ('No, I'm normal') — teach them 'Thank you, I practiced a lot'
Saying 'sorry' is rare unless truly at fault or afraid of consequences
If they ignore you, they're not mad — they just have bad emotion. Don't take it personally.
Very smart people until they're not — then short-sighted. Very heavy on credentials (even if faked/redundant). Trust ideas based on merit alone is rare.
Face culture weaponized by scam English centers — no one complains publicly, they just quietly switch

content: Vietnamese English centers hire attractive white faces (often Russian, $800–1,200/mo, bad English) to deceive parents who can't speak English
Fake certificates, fake progression, 'eternal student' model — product is keeping students enrolled forever, not graduating them
Parents spend 30–50% of household income on lessons that produce zero real fluency
No one complains because of face culture — they stay quiet and go through revolving door of eternal students
Our counter-move: results over appearance, employer dashboards, graduation timelines, 10-100x cheaper and infinitely more effective

our_graduation_standard.intensive: 1 year — student doesn't need us anymore
our_graduation_standard.max: 2 years — even for lazy students with roadblocks
our_graduation_standard.philosophy: I want my students to graduate. Scam centers want to keep the illusion of progress and keep students in the revolving door as long as they can.

graduation_timeline.quote: I want my students to graduate. I want my students in the intense program to not need me after a year. I want my students, like if they're in the more laid-back program, a year and a half. I want them to graduate. If they're languages aren't their forte, and they're a little bit lazy, and they have some other roadblocks, maybe two years. But I can't see them needing more than two years if I'm doing something properly.
